direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale is good, as he uses his experience directing the first one to translate the animated Berk into this live-action version to give the world more depth and make it look more realistic; They effectively translate the flight and action sequences to the live-action world, as they look more realistic with the advanced technology and real-world sets; The direction on a microscale is exactly the same as the first movie, as almost all of the scenes are a shot-for-shot remake of the first movie; The storytelling is exactly the same as the first movie, as it is a shot-for-shot remake, but it does use its 30 minutes of extra runtime to slow down the pace and make the story breathe a little more

performance.comments: He holds his own and plays the teenage Hiccup well; it's pretty on par with the original
Given more material than the original character, and it does a decent job with it; It has decent chemistry with Thames
The only returning actor from the original movie makes the most of his experience as he picks up where he left off to bring Stoick to life in live-action form
Uses his experience playing similar characters well as he has good comedic relief and plays a mentor figure well to Hiccup

cast.comments: Everyone feels rightly cast and helps support the main cast and move the story forward

story.comments: The concept is literally a shot-for-shot remake of the original, with most of the scenes and dialogue being the exact same; The plot structure is the exact same as the original movie, but at a slower pace to allow the scenes to breathe more; The character writing is the exact same as the original movie, a "Dances with Wolves"-esque teen learning to live with the dragons despite his father and tribe wanting to kill them

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is almost the exact same as the original, making this basically a shot-for-shot remake of the original; The humor is the same as the original; The symbolism is the exact same as the original movie, but still profound in showing the father-son dynamic between two generations with different morals; The foreshadowing is the same as the original, but it is even worse considering this movie is a shot-for-shot remake so you know exactly what's going to happen if you watched the original

score.comments: Basically, the same as the original, but it is still used well to make the movie feel like an extension of the original and help build this world

cinematography.comments: It helps capture the world and is used well to basically mimic all the shots from the original movie

editing.comments: Editing feels sharp and clean as it seamlessly stitches together the higher-production shots this time around

sound.comments: Makes the movie feel grand and makes the movie feel more realistic; something you wish for with a higher production budget and real-world sets

visual_effects.comments: Uses updated technology to help provide more depth to Berk and make the world look more realistic; I was not a huge fan of the dragon designs because it took away from the adorable charm of the original movies

production_design.comments: It feels more natural and real, as the real sets and advanced technology paint more depth in Berk than the original movie could at the time

makeup.comments: Helps bring to life the Vikings from the original movie

costumes.comments: Helps make the characters emulate the originals and look like Norse Vikings

review.pacing: Pacing is a lot better this time around because they use the extra 30 minutes of runtime to really slow things down and let scenes breathe;
review.climax: Climax is executed well as it does not feel as rushed as the original movie and used more advanced CGI technology to paint the scene; Despite these improvements, the climax is literally exactly the same as the original
review.tone: Tone is the same as the original, heavily influenced by Norse and dragon mythology and this being a family movie
review.final_notes: What they should have done was release a remastered version of the original with enhanced CGI and additional scenes (but that would make no money); this is a well-made movie, it is just not necessary
review.overall: Overall, a pretty good movie that uses its longer runtime and modern CGI to improve on the rushed pace and dated animation of the original movie, but it is almost a shot-for-shot remake without adding anything new; what they should have done was release a remastered version of the original How to Train Your Dragon with updated graphics and additional scenes, but that would also make no money
